package_info.why_malicious: The hijacked PHPass package was modified to include code that exfiltrates AWS credentials and environment variables to an external Heroku endpoint. This results in credential theft and exposes users to potential compromise of their AWS infrastructure.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (when the PasswordHash class is instantiated), the code reads the AWS_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables, then sends their values to a hardcoded Heroku endpoint via HTTP GET, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code explicitly accesses sensitive AWS credentials from environment variables and transmits them to an external, attacker-controlled server. This is a direct credential theft technique and is not expected in any legitimate password hashing library.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal password hashing library should never access AWS credentials or any unrelated environment secrets, nor should it make unsolicited network requests to external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code may access environment variables for configuration purposes, but it should never exfiltrate secrets to third-party endpoints or make network requests containing sensitive data.
key_indicators: Access to AWS_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables
Network request containing sensitive credential values
Unexpected network activity in a password hashing library

attack_chain.action: Attacker takes over the abandoned PHPass package via repo-jacking on Packagist.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious versions of the PHPass package.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is added to the package to steal AWS credentials from environment variables and exfiltrate them to an external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft upon package installation or use.

attack_chain.action: Victim installs or updates the compromised PHPass package, triggering the malicious code during class instantiation.
attack_chain.leads_to: AWS credentials are sent to the attacker's Heroku endpoint.

attack_chain.action: Attacker receives the exfiltrated AWS credentials, enabling potential unauthorized access to victim AWS resources.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: unauthorized access and potential compromise of AWS infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Access to AWS_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables in third-party PHP libraries
Unsolicited HTTP/HTTPS requests to external endpoints during package import or class instantiation
Network requests containing environment variable values associated with cloud credentials
file_indicators: src/HauteLook/Phpass/PasswordHash.php containing getenv or file_get_contents with external URLs
Any dependency package code that reads AWS credentials and initiates network requests
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to Herokuapp domains from build or runtime environments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Use static analysis to flag third-party PHP packages that access AWS credential environment variables (e.g., getenv('AWS_ACCESS_KEY'), getenv('AWS_SECRET_KEY')) and make outbound network requests (e.g., file_get_contents, curl) to untrusted domains. Monitor network logs for HTTP requests to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com or similar suspicious endpoints, especially from build, CI/CD, or runtime environments. Alert on any password hashing library exhibiting network activity or credential access.
